name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Fundamental physical quantities in classical mechanics

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding basic physical concepts in mechanics:

List I (Concept / Quantity) List II (Description / Definition)
A. Inertia I. Product of mass and velocity of a body
B. Linear momentum II. Inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion
C. Impulse of a force III. Product of average force and time duration, equal to change in momentum
D. Centripetal acceleration IV. Inward radial acceleration experienced during uniform circular motion, given by \( \frac{v^2}{R} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual definitions of the quantities
The fundamental physical quantities in Newtonian mechanics are defined as follows:

  • Inertia is the inherent property of an object by virtue of which it resists any attempt to change its state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line. Therefore, inertia corresponds to the inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion.
  • Linear momentum of a body is defined as the product of its mass and velocity, mathematically represented as \( p = mv \).
  • Impulse measures the overall effect of a force acting over a time interval. By the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse equals the product of average force and time interval, which is identical to the resulting change in linear momentum, \( J = F_{\text{avg}} \Delta t = \Delta p \).
  • Centripetal acceleration is the inward radial acceleration required to keep a body moving along a curved circular path of radius \( R \) at speed \( v \), given by \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \).

Step 2: Matching each pair
Pairing each item according to its physical definition:

  • Inertia matches with the inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion (A-II).
  • Linear momentum matches with the product of mass and velocity of a body (B-I).
  • Impulse of a force matches with the product of average force and time duration, equal to change in momentum (C-III).
  • Centripetal acceleration matches with the inward radial acceleration experienced during uniform circular motion (D-IV).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Characteristics and properties of various frictions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the characteristics of different types of friction:

List I (Type of Friction) List II (Characteristic Feature)
A. Static friction I. Maximum threshold value given by \( \mu_s N \) beyond which sliding starts
B. Limiting friction II. Resistance arising due to momentary deformation of surfaces in contact when an object rolls
C. Kinetic friction III. Opposes actual relative sliding between contact surfaces and is nearly independent of sliding speed
D. Rolling friction IV. Self-adjusting resistive force that opposes impending motion and satisfies \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual principles of friction
The laws and features governing frictional forces in mechanics are:

  • Static friction is a self-adjusting contact force that comes into play when there is an applied force attempting to cause relative motion. It opposes impending relative motion and increases from zero up to a maximum threshold value, satisfying \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \).
  • Limiting friction is the maximum possible static frictional force that surfaces can exert before sliding begins, given by \( f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N \).
  • Kinetic friction comes into play when there is actual relative sliding motion between two contact surfaces. It opposes the relative motion and remains nearly independent of the relative sliding velocity over a wide range of speeds.
  • Rolling friction arises when a spherical or cylindrical body rolls over a surface. Because of contact pressure, momentary deformation of the surfaces occurs, causing a small resistance to rolling motion that is much smaller than kinetic friction.

Step 2: Matching each pair
Connecting each type of friction to its characteristic property:

  • Static friction matches with the self-adjusting resistive force that opposes impending motion and satisfies \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \) (A-IV).
  • Limiting friction matches with the maximum threshold value given by \( \mu_s N \) beyond which sliding starts (B-I).
  • Kinetic friction matches with opposing actual relative sliding and being nearly independent of sliding speed (C-III).
  • Rolling friction matches with the resistance arising due to momentary deformation of surfaces in contact when an object rolls (D-II).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Governing equations for various mechanical systems

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the dynamics of circular motion on roads:

List I (Physical Situation) List II (Mathematical Expression)
A. Maximum safe speed on an unbanked level circular road of radius \( R \) I. \( \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \)
B. Optimum speed on a banked circular road where no frictional force is needed II. \( \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \)
C. Maximum permissible speed on a banked circular road with friction coefficient \( \mu_s \) III. \( \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \)
D. Banking angle \( \theta \) designed for a vehicle travelling at speed \( v \) IV. \( \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Derivations for circular motion on roads
Let us examine the force balance for each case:

  • On an unbanked horizontal circular road of radius \( R \), the centripetal force is provided entirely by static friction: \( f_s = \frac{m v^2}{R} \). Since \( f_s \le \mu_s N = \mu_s mg \), the maximum safe speed is \( v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \).
  • On a banked road of inclination \( \theta \), the horizontal component of normal reaction \( N \sin\theta \) provides centripetal acceleration, while \( N \cos\theta = mg \). When no lateral frictional force is called upon, the speed is optimum: \( \frac{N \sin\theta}{N \cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \frac{v_0^2}{R g} \implies v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \).
  • When a vehicle moves at the maximum possible speed on a banked road, friction acts downward along the slope. Balancing horizontal and vertical forces gives \( N \sin\theta + f_s \cos\theta = \frac{m v_{\max}^2}{R} \) and \( N \cos\theta - f_s \sin\theta = mg \). Substituting \( f_s = \mu_s N \) yields \( v_{\max} = \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \).
  • To design a road so that vehicles rounding a curve of radius \( R \) at speed \( v \) experience zero wear and tear from friction, the banking angle must satisfy \( \tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{R g} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \).

Step 2: Matching each situation with its expression
Connecting each circular motion scenario to its formula:

  • Maximum safe speed on an unbanked level circular road matches with \( \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \) (A-II).
  • Optimum speed on a banked circular road with zero friction matches with \( \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \) (B-IV).
  • Maximum permissible speed on a banked circular road with friction matches with \( \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \) (C-I).
  • Banking angle designed for a speed \( v \) matches with \( \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \) (D-III).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Apparent weight in different accelerated frames

questiontext.text:
A person of mass \( m \) stands on a weighing scale placed on the floor of an elevator. Match List-I with List-II regarding the apparent weight \( R \) recorded by the scale in various states of motion:

List I (Motion of Elevator) List II (Reading of Weighing Scale \( R \))
A. Accelerating upwards with a constant acceleration \( a \) I. \( R = m(g - a) \)
B. Accelerating downwards with a constant acceleration \( a \) (where \( a < g \)) II. \( R = 0 \) (State of weightlessness)
C. Elevator cable breaks and it falls freely under gravity (\( a = g \)) III. \( R = m(g + a) \)
D. Moving upwards or downwards with a constant velocity \( v \) IV. \( R = mg \) (True gravitational weight)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Free-body diagram and equations of motion
Let \( R \) be the normal reaction force exerted by the scale on the person, and \( mg \) be the downward gravitational force. The reading of the scale equals \( R \).

  • When the elevator accelerates upwards with acceleration \( a \), the net upward force is \( R - mg = ma \). Solving for the apparent weight gives \( R = m(g + a) \).
  • When the elevator accelerates downwards with acceleration \( a < g \), the net downward force is \( mg - R = ma \). Solving for the apparent weight gives \( R = m(g - a) \).
  • When the lift falls freely under gravity, the downward acceleration is \( a = g \). The equation of motion becomes \( mg - R = mg \implies R = m(g - g) = 0 \), corresponding to the condition of weightlessness.
  • When the elevator moves with constant velocity (either upwards or downwards), the net acceleration is zero (\( a = 0 \)). The equation of motion gives \( R - mg = 0 \implies R = mg \), which equals the person's true gravitational weight.

Step 2: Matching each motion to the resulting apparent weight
Matching each case:

  • Accelerating upwards with acceleration \( a \) matches with \( R = m(g + a) \) (A-III).
  • Accelerating downwards with acceleration \( a < g \) matches with \( R = m(g - a) \) (B-I).
  • Falling freely under gravity matches with \( R = 0 \), the state of weightlessness (C-II).
  • Moving with constant velocity matches with \( R = mg \), the true gravitational weight (D-IV).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.
